medications.sig: 1 drop in each eye up to four times daily as needed for dryness

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology group. Visit 01/16/2024.

Referred for intermittent blurred vision and dry, gritty eyes in a patient with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis.

Visual acuity 20/20 each eye with near correction not required. Pupils equal, no afferent defect. Intraocular pressures normal. Slit lamp: lids and lashes normal; conjunctiva quiet; reduced tear film break-up time both eyes with mild punctate staining inferiorly; anterior chamber deep and quiet, no cells or flare; no keratic precipitates; iris without nodules. Dilated exam: clear vitreous, normal optic discs, macula and vessels normal, no periphlebitis or choroidal lesions.

Impression: no evidence of uveitis or posterior segment sarcoidosis. Ocular surface dryness, likely accounting for the fluctuating blur with reading.
Plan: preservative-free carboxymethylcellulose artificial tears up to four times daily, screen breaks when grading. Yearly eye exam given her sarcoidosis, sooner for redness, pain or light sensitivity.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Eye doctor letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news from the eye doctor: no inflammation inside the eyes from the sarcoid. The blur seems to be from dry eyes, so use the artificial tears they recommended. They want to see you once a year.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up.

Eyes better with the drops, blur only at the end of long grading nights. Energy so-so, better on weekends. Occasional dry cough, nothing new. No fevers. Shins clear since January. UC quiet.

Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g BID, artificial tears prn. NKDA.

Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Skin clear.

A/P: sarcoidosis, stable on observation; calcium recheck today. Ophthalmology yearly. Pulmonology follow-up is overdue; she will call them. UC: continue mesalamine. RTC at physical in September.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: Gastroenterology, office visit 06/04/2024. Ulcerative colitis in sustained clinical remission on mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily. No rectal bleeding, one or two formed stools daily. Sarcoidosis followed by pulmonology. Abdomen benign. Plan: continue mesalamine; renewed prescription for one year with refills. Return in one year. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Annual. Weight back up to 69.6 kg. Feels about as good as she has in a couple of years. Cough rare. Eyes fine with drops. UC quiet, saw GI in June. Has not rescheduled pulmonology; given their number again.

Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g BID, carboxymethylcellulose drops prn. NKDA. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well. Eyes quiet. Neck no adenopathy. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Shins clear. Neuro nonfocal.

Plan: CMP, UA. District health form completed: no restrictions. Flu and COVID in October. Pap next due 2028. Mammogram to start at 40.

orders.reason: right peripheral facial weakness in sarcoidosis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt texted: right side of face feels heavy and her smile is crooked, building for about a week. No arm or leg weakness, speech clear, no headache. Coworker noticed it. Triage: gradual, face only, more than a week. Same-day slot at her lunch break 12:10.

documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About a week of gradually worsening right facial weakness. Started as trouble whistling and a droop at the corner of her mouth, now the right eye doesn't close all the way and it waters. No limb weakness, numbness, vision loss, speech or swallowing trouble, no ear pain or vesicles. Dry cough has crept back over the last couple of months, some breathlessness. No fever.

Exam: vitals normal. Right facial weakness involving forehead, eye closure and mouth; left side normal. No vesicles in the ear canal. Other cranial nerves intact. Strength and sensation normal in all four limbs, reflexes symmetric, gait normal.

A/P: right peripheral facial nerve palsy, progressive over a week, in a patient with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis; facial nerve involvement from sarcoid is a real possibility. No central signs. Urgent neurology referral, office called directly and fit her in 12/16. Eye protection now: artificial tears through the day, tape the lid closed at night. Return or ED for any limb weakness, speech change or a severe headache.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology clinic. Consultation 12/16/2024.

Reason: right facial weakness, urgent referral from primary care.

She is 37, with biopsy-confirmed sarcoidosis (pulmonary and nodal), ulcerative colitis and a prior parathyroid adenoma, last seen by her physician a year ago for fatigue and eye complaints. Three weeks of progressive weakness of the right face. Two months of persistent dry cough with occasional breathlessness. No fever, weight loss or night sweats.

Medications: mesalamine; artificial tears. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with sarcoidosis, mother with lupus, father with type 2 diabetes, paternal cousin with ulcerative colitis.

Examination: right lower motor neuron facial palsy with drooping of the mouth, incomplete closure of the right eye and inability to raise the right eyebrow. Remaining cranial nerves normal. Motor, sensory, reflexes and coordination normal. Lungs without wheezes, rales or rhonchi.

Labs: calcium 11.2 mg/dL, ACE elevated, CBC normal, ANA negative, RF negative.
Chest radiograph: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

Impression: right facial nerve palsy attributed to neurosarcoidosis, the most common cranial neuropathy in sarcoid.
Plan: protect the right cornea with lubricating drops during the day and taping at night; eye patch outdoors on windy days. Expect gradual recovery over weeks to months. Return if new cranial nerve or limb symptoms develop.

documents.title: Eye taping
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neurology said this is from the sarcoid and should get better on its own over time. The taping at night is awkward. Is there a better tape to use? And can I keep using the same drops all day?

documents.title: RE: Eye taping
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Paper surgical tape from any pharmacy works best and is gentle on the skin; close the lid fully, then tape horizontally across it. Yes, the same artificial tears are fine as often as you need during the day. Call if the eye becomes red or painful or your vision changes.

documents.title: Neurology note received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Neurology consult 12/16/24 received 1/6, scanned and routed to PCP. Pt has f/u here 2/11.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up right facial palsy (neurosarcoid per neurology 12/16).

Slowly coming back: can close the eye now with effort, still tapes at night. Smile still a little lopsided. Eye not red or painful. Cough settled again.

Exam: right face with mild residual weakness, eye closes fully with effort, forehead moves partially. Cornea clear by penlight. Lungs clear. Remainder nonfocal.

A/P: improving facial palsy. Keep lubricating until full closure without effort. Calcium today. Recheck at physical; neurology as needed.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I move my physical to after school gets out? Mid to late June works best. Also my face is basically back to normal, I stopped taping a few weeks ago.

documents.title: RE: Scheduling

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, first week of summer break.

Face fully recovered; stopped taping in April and only uses drops occasionally. Cough gone for now. Energy decent. UC quiet, sees GI this month. No joint complaints.

Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g BID, artificial tears prn. NKDA. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: symmetric facial movement, eye closure complete. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Skin clear. No synovitis.

Plan: facial palsy resolved. CMP, CBC with diff, lipids. Flu and COVID in the fall. Ophthalmology yearly visit due; reminded.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look stable: calcium still a touch high as it has been, kidney function, blood counts and cholesterol all normal. Enjoy the summer.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza and 2025-26 COVID vaccines given IM, one in each deltoid. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: Triage call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called after school. Two weeks of right knee pain and swelling, now the left ankle too, getting worse; low-grade temps to about 100 at home; a rash on her lower legs. Limping, hard to stand at the board. No injury. Bowels normal.

A hot swollen knee with fever needs the joint tapped to exclude infection today or tomorrow; we cannot do that safely in the office this evening. Advised ED. She will go first thing in the morning if tonight's temp stays under 101, tonight if higher or if she can't bear weight.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Physician record, 12/11/2025.

CC: right knee and left ankle pain and swelling.

HPI: 38-year-old woman with sarcoidosis, ulcerative colitis, a past parathyroid problem and a prior facial nerve palsy. Two weeks of increasing pain and swelling of the right knee, then the left ankle, with low-grade fevers at home and a rash on both lower legs. No trauma, no tick bite she knows of, no new sexual partner, no urinary or eye symptoms. Her colitis is well controlled on mesalamine.

Meds: mesalamine, artificial tears. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 37.9 C, HR 92, BP 124/78, RR 16, SpO2 99%. Right knee warm with effusion, motion limited by pain. Left ankle warm and swollen, similar. No deformity. Pustular rash over both lower legs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Arthrocentesis, right knee, lateral approach, sterile technique, after consent: about 25 mL cloudy yellow fluid. Tolerated well.

Results: hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, WBC 9,800/uL. ESR 45 mm/h. CRP 3.2 mg/dL. RF negative, ANA negative. Synovial fluid WBC 16,400/uL, no crystals, Gram stain without organisms; culture pending at discharge.
Radiographs right knee and left ankle: soft tissue swelling only, no joint space narrowing, erosions or osteopenia.

MDM: inflammatory oligoarthritis of large lower-extremity joints in a patient with ulcerative colitis; synovial count and Gram stain do not suggest septic arthritis. Most consistent with enteropathic (IBD-associated) peripheral arthritis. NSAIDs avoided given her colitis.

Disposition: discharged. Acetaminophen for pain, rest and ice. Follow up with primary care this week and rheumatology. Return for fever above 101, a hotter or more swollen joint, or inability to bear weight. The lab will call if the culture grows.

documents.title: ED culture result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called by the hospital lab: right knee fluid culture no growth at 72 hours. Pt informed; knee still swollen but fever gone. Post-ED visit stays 12/16.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 12/11 for a swollen right knee and left ankle with fevers. ED record received: knee tapped, synovial WBC 16,400, no crystals, Gram stain negative; culture final no growth. ESR 45, CRP 3.2 mg/dL, RF and ANA negative. X-rays soft tissue swelling only. ED dx enteropathic (IBD-related) arthritis.

Now: no fever since the weekend. Knee less tight after the tap, still sore on stairs; ankle swollen in the evenings. Pain 4/10 with acetaminophen. The rash on her legs is fading. UC quiet, no bleeding.

Exam: afebrile. Right knee with a small effusion, warm, flexion to about 100 degrees. Left ankle mildly swollen and tender. Lower legs with a few fading spots. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Enteropathic peripheral arthritis with UC. Rheumatology referral, asked for the soonest slot. Acetaminophen as needed; avoid ibuprofen and naproxen because of the colitis. Out of work rest of this week; note given.
2. UC: let GI know about the arthritis; she will message them.
3. Sarcoidosis, hypercalcemia: unchanged plan.

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacist called: filled sulfasalazine DR 500 mg from outside rheumatology on 1/14 (1 BID x 7 days then 2 BID), and their system flagged it alongside mesalamine. Wanted to confirm we are aware of both. We had no rheumatology note yet. Per PCP: rheumatology and GI manage these; the overlap is a known combination, OK to dispense both. Added sulfasalazine to med list as an outside prescription. Rheumatology office asked for their note and lab plan.

documents.title: Rheumatology office callback
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Rheumatology office returned call: they want CBC and CMP at 2-4 weeks, then every 3 months while on sulfasalazine, drawn here and faxed to them. Letter to follow. Lab-only visit booked 2/10.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sulfasalazine 4-week labs: blood counts normal including neutrophils, liver enzymes and kidney function normal. Calcium mildly elevated as usual. Faxed to rheumatology. Portal note sent to patient.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Visit 01/14/2026.

Referred after an ED visit for oligoarthritis of the right knee and left ankle. Known to us from 2023 for sarcoidosis. Joint symptoms since late November with fevers; ED synovial fluid inflammatory without crystals or infection, culture negative, ESR and CRP elevated, RF and ANA negative, radiographs without erosions.

Now: right knee and left ankle still painful and swollen by evening, morning stiffness under an hour. UC quiet on mesalamine. No back pain, no eye redness.

Exam: small right knee effusion, mild left ankle synovitis. No other joint involvement. Skin clear.

Assessment: peripheral enteropathic arthritis, large-joint, associated with ulcerative colitis.
Plan: start sulfasalazine 500 mg twice daily for one week, then 1000 mg twice daily. Discussed with her gastroenterologist; mesalamine continues. CBC and CMP at 2-4 weeks and every 3 months, drawn with primary care. Avoid NSAIDs. Follow up in 3 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology. Follow-up 04/15/2026.

On sulfasalazine 1000 mg twice daily since late January with mild nausea in the first week only. Knee and ankle swelling have settled; she is back to full days at school without limping. No new joints.

Exam: no effusion at the right knee, full range; left ankle without synovitis.

Monitoring labs from 02/10 normal.

Assessment: enteropathic peripheral arthritis, in remission on sulfasalazine.
Plan: continue sulfasalazine 1000 mg twice daily; labs every 3 months with primary care; return in 6 months.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 3-month sulfasalazine labs normal: counts, liver and kidney tests. Calcium unchanged at its usual mildly elevated level. Faxed to rheumatology.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. School out last week.

Joints quiet since spring on sulfasalazine; rheumatology happy. No fevers. Occasional dry cough, nothing new. Face normal. Eyes fine, uses drops now and then; has not seen ophthalmology this year, will book. UC no flares, GI visit coming up next month.

Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g BID, sulfasalazine 1000 mg BID, artificial tears prn. NKDA. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well. Facial movement symmetric. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Joints without effusion or warmth. Shins clear.

Plan: UA today; blood work drawn in May is current. Next sulfasalazine labs in August. Flu and COVID this fall. Mammogram screening at 40 next February; order placed at the next visit. Follow-up in September for sarcoid and calcium.

documents.title: Labs before school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Teacher PD days start next week. Can I do my August blood work at the September appointment instead? Also the pharmacy says my sulfasalazine refills are done, rheumatology already sent a new one so just FYI.

documents.title: RE: Labs before school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, we can draw everything at the September visit. Thanks for the heads-up on the refill.
